articles.title: La historia del discreto Mercedes de Jenson Button que era más caro y corría más que un Ferrari
articles.standfirst: El piloto británico tuvo durante 15 años un exclusivo pero discreto Mercedes que alcanzaba 320 km/h costaba y que en 2004 le costó 236.000 euros
articles.summary: El piloto británico tuvo durante 15 años un exclusivo pero discreto Mercedes que alcanzaba 320 km/h costaba y costaba más que un Porsche 911 Turbo o un Ferrari 360 Modena
articles.body: Jenson Button se compró en diciembre de 2004 un Mercedes CLK que mantuvo hasta 2019. Solo que no se trataba de un CLK de los que por entonces uno podía comprar en cualquier concesionario Mercedes, sino de un CLK DTM AMG, un coche muy especial que solo se vendió a clientes muy especiales. Para entender de dónde salió este coche hay que remontarse a los éxitos de Mercedes en el DTM, el campeonato alemán de turismos. La marca dominó la categoría en 2002 y 2003, y Bernd Schneider se proclamó campeón de pilotos en esta última temporada al volante del CLK de competición. El equipo ganó nueve de las diez carreras disputadas, y este resultado llevó a AMG a proponer una versión de calle que celebrase aquellos triunfos y trasladase parte de la tecnología de los circuitos a la carretera. La dirección de Mercedes dio luz verde al proyecto y los ingenieros de Affalterbach (el pueblo alemán donde se montan a mano los AMG) se pusieron manos a la obra. Los pilotos oficiales de AMG acumularon más de 30.000 km de pruebas en carreteras y circuitos para poner a punto el nuevo modelo, que tomó como referencia el coche con el que Schneider había conquistado el campeonato. El resultado fue un coupé que incluso superaba en potencia a su hermano de carreras. Bajo el capó escondía un V8 de 5.439 centímetros cúbicos, que entregaba 582 CV y 800 Nm de par máximo. La transmisión automática AMG Speedshift de cinco velocidades enviaba la fuerza al eje trasero y permitía cambiar de marcha mediante levas situadas detrás del volante. Las prestaciones estaban a la altura de los mejores superdeportivos del momento. El CLK DTM AMG aceleraba de 0 a 100 km/h en 3,9 segundos y alcanzaba los 320 km/h... ¡y eso que tenía limitador electrónico! Para poner toda esa potencia bajo control, incorporaba una suspensión casi de competición, con amortiguadores regulables en altura y elementos más rígidos que los que pudiera llevar cualquier otro CLK de calle (a excepción de los GT1 de resistencia), un diferencial autoblocante mecánico, discos de material compuesto y un programa de estabilidad ESP adaptado a tanto potencial. La carrocería recibió muchos elementos de fibra de carbono, además de pasos de rueda ensanchados para cubrir unas llantas de 19 pulgadas delante y 20 detrás, un frontal con grandes tomas de aire y un alerón trasero de generosas dimensiones. En el interior desaparecían las plazas traseras para dejar espacio a un entramado de barras antivuelco de carbono, y las dos butacas eran de tipo bacquet, tapizadas en cuero y Alcantara. Como colofón, una placa en la consola central recordaba la exclusividad del modelo con la inscripción 'CLK DTM One out of 100'. Mercedes puso a su CLK DTM AMG un precio de 236.060 euros cuando llegó al mercado en 2004. Si hoy nos parece un precio desorbitado, imagínate entonces, cuando un Ferrari 360 Modena, con su motor V8 atmosférico de 400 CV y sus 295 km/h, partía de unos 128.200 euros. Incluso el Ferrari 575M Maranello, un V12 de 515 CV, salía en España por unos 224.956 euros en 2004. Entre los afortunados propietarios del CLK DTM estaban Kimi Räikkönen, Takuma Sato y Jenson Button, dueño del coche que ves en estas imágenes. El británico, como hemos comentado, lo retuvo hasta 2019, cuando se lo vendió a un coleccionista japonés. Pero este segundo propietario ha decidido 'renovar' su garaje e Iconic Auctioneers lo va a sacar a subasta este 14 de noviembre. El coche, por cierto, no tiene más que 18.114 km y se espera que su próximo propietario pague entre 480.000 y 600.000 euros. Todo, por su escasez, su filosofía casi de competición y por haber pertenecido a un campeón del mundo de Fórmula 1.

articles.title: India's 20-year-old chess grandmaster Pranav V crowned World Junior Blitz champion after Rapid silver
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: 20-year-old Indian Grandmaster Pranav Venkatesh, who became FIDE World Junior Champion in the classical time-control last year, has now
articles.body: NEW DELHI: 20-year-old Indian Grandmaster Pranav Venkatesh, who became FIDE World Junior Champion in the classical time-control last year, has now clinched the Open section title at the FIDE World Junior Blitz Championship, finishing on an impressive 10.5 points from 13 rounds in UAE on Friday.Pranav topped the final standings, finishing a full point ahead of three players who shared second place with 9.5 points each.Kyrgyzstan’s International Master Eldiyar Orozbaev secured second place, while Armenia’s IM Robert Piliposyan finished third. Syria’s FIDE Master Mazen Fandi also scored 9.5 points to take fourth place.Uzbekistan’s GM Mukhammadzokhid Suyarov, FIDE’s GM Erdem Khubukshanov and Uzbekistan’s GM Khumoyun Begmuratov followed with nine points apiece.Pranav had made a strong start to the championship, ending the first day of blitz tied at the top of the Open leaderboard with six points.He carried that momentum into the remaining rounds to emerge as the outright champion.There was also Indian representation among the leading players in the Girls section.WIM Aamuktha Guntaka finished fifth with nine points from 13 rounds, while IM Savitha Shri B secured 8.5 points to take seventh place.The Girls title went to WGM Valeria Kleymenova, who scored 10 points. Uzbekistan’s WGM Afruza Khamdamova and Russia’s WFM Veronika Iudina finished second and third respectively, both with 9.5 points.Pranav's blitz triumph adds to an encouraging campaignPranav’s blitz triumph adds to an encouraging campaign at the World Junior Rapid and Blitz Championships in Al Ain.He had earlier won silver in the Open section of the World Junior Rapid Championship, scoring seven points from nine rounds. articles.title: José Cuadrado, experto en tecnología, avisa sobre WhatsApp: “Está gastando memoria y no te das cuenta”
articles.standfirst: El especialista ha explicado cómo evitar esto
articles.summary: El especialista ha explicado cómo evitar esto
articles.body: Dentro de teléfono móvil hay muchas aplicaciones que ocupan memoria, pero una de las que más lo hace, y además sin darnos cuenta, es WhatsApp. Pues bien, José Cuadrado, experto en tecnología, ha explicado cómo evitar esto a través de un vídeo publicado en sus redes sociales. “Atención a esto, ¿sabías que WhatsApp podría estar ocupando varias gigas de almacenamiento en tu móvil y tú no te estás dando ni cuenta? Y lo peor es que buena parte de ese espacio lo están ocupando fotos y vídeos que te mandaron hace años. Te voy a enseñar dónde encontrarlos, cómo borrarlos y cómo evitar que esto vuelva a ocurrir”, comienza diciendo el también coordinador digital en la Cadena COPE. Cuadrado ha explicado que “WhatsApp no tiene una papelera general como la que pueda tener tu ordenador, pero sí una herramienta que mucha gente desconoce y que permite localizar los archivos que más memoria te están consumiendo”. “Vamos a comprobarlo. Abre WhatsApp, entra en ajustes, después en almacenamiento, almacenamiento y datos y pulsa administrar almacenamiento”, detallaba. “Aquí puedes comprobar cuánto espacio te está ocupando WhatsApp y los archivos más pesados. También aparecen las conversaciones y los grupos que más memoria te están consumiendo”, apunta el experto en la materia. Pero “lo interesante es que puedes entrar en cualquiera de esos apartados”, seleccionar los vídeos, fotografías o documentos que ya no necesitas, y pulsa el icono de papelera. Por si esto fuera poco, el especialista tecnológico ha dejado un último truco. “Vuelve a almacenamiento y entra en descarga automática de archivos. Ahí puedes decidir qué fotos, vídeos o documentos se descargan o no automáticamente y con esto controlas el almacenamiento de tu dispositivo”, sentenciaba.

articles.title: Giants trade Reiver Sanmartin for Robert Cranz
articles.summary: An interesting arm heads to AAA.
articles.body:
The San Francisco Giants announced a small deal on Friday, as a trickle down from Monday's roster-cutting actions. Lefty reliever Reiver Sanmartin has been traded to the Washington Nationals in exchange for Minor League reliever Robert Cranz.

It's not news that Sanmartin is gone, as the Giants announced that he had been designated for assignment on Monday, amongst the flurry of moves that got the roster back down to 40 players at the deadline. But most DFA'd players leave with nothing in return, so it's nice that Sanmartin was an exception, and the Giants were able to get something back to allow the Nationals to jump to the front of the line.

As is always the case with these sorts of deals, it's not a huge haul they got back, but Cranz is interesting. The 23-year old right-hander was drafted in the seventh round of the 2024 draft (pick No. 200 on the dot) out of Oklahoma State, and received a mildly underslot bonus of $190,000. He performed fairly well in Low-A and High-A in his first full season in 2025, and started to make a name for himself in 2026.

Cranz opened the year in High-A, where he had a 2.25 ERA and a 2.68 FIP, with a whopping 27 strikeouts in just 16 innings. He kept it up in AA, where he posted a 3.42 ERA and a 2.95 FIP, with 40 strikeouts in 26.1 innings.

A native of Keller, Texas, Cranz made it to AAA to end the year, and that's where his success ended. It was a rude introduction to the top ring of the Minors, and he ended his cup of coffee there with a 13.11 ERA, a 7.17 FIP, and just nine strikeouts in 11.2 innings.

Cranz mostly throws hard stuff, as in AAA he used his four-seam fastball (which averaged 95.2 mph) nearly half of the time, while throwing his cutter and slider more than 20% of the time each. There's definitely something intriguing there, and he'll be a big part of AAA Sacramento's bullpen depth this year, and have a chance to play his way into the Majors.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers’ Brother Jordan Makes Unexpected Admission After Years of Family Tension: ‘I Trust the Guy’
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers is receiving public praise from his younger brother, Jordan Rodgers, following years of tension within their family. During an ESPN appearance...
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers is receiving public praise from his younger brother, Jordan Rodgers , following years of tension within their family.

During an ESPN appearance on Wednesday, November 4, Jordan complimented the Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback 's experience and ability to lead his team into the playoffs, according to an Entertainment Weekly article published on Friday, November 6.

"This one might surprise you a little bit," Jordan, 38, said before naming his brother as his pick for the most dependable quarterback, per the report.

He explained that the Pittsburgh Steelers ' strong defense and running game allow Aaron to focus on managing the offense rather than carrying the entire team.

"I just feel like I trust the guy that's got the MVPs, that has the veteran status, that's seen everything," Jordan said.

The comments come months after Aaron, 42, began reconnecting with relatives following a family rift that lasted more than a decade.

In July, Aaron shared photos, via Instagram , with his parents, Ed Rodgers and Darla Rodgers , and older brother Luke Rodgers . Per the report, Jordan and his wife, JoJo Fletcher , were not pictured at the gathering but liked the post.

As First for Sports previously reported , Aaron discussed repairing his family relationships during a September appearance on the Not Just Football podcast.

"There were tough conversations for sure," he admitted on the podcast, adding that he was in a "much better headspace."

The quarterback also credited his wife, Brittani — whose identity has not been shared publicly — for supporting him through the reconciliation, during the podcast appearance.

However, according to Page Six , a source said Jordan's relationship with Aaron remains complicated. "It still seems like a very sensitive topic for Jordan," the source said.

According to Entertainment Weekly , the brothers' strained relationship became public in 2016 when Jordan discussed their lack of contact while competing for Fletcher's heart on season 12 of ABC's reality dating show The Bachelorette .

Aaron and the Steelers currently lead the AFC North with a 6-2 record and are riding a four-game winning streak as they prepare to face the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, November 15, per the team's official website .

articles.title: Saquon Barkley set to play as Eagles remain without DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks
articles.summary: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley is on track to play against his former team.
articles.body:
Eagles running back Saquon Barkley is on track to play against his former team.

Barkley remained limited in practice on Friday with hamstring and back injuries, but he has no injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants. Barkley missed a couple of games with the hamstring injury and has been limited to 32 offensive snaps the last two weeks.

While quarterback Joe Milton will have Barkley with him in the backfield for his first Eagles start, he'll be missing wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). Smith and Wicks are both going to miss their third straight game.

Linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring, quad), defensive back Michael Carter (abdomen), wide receiver Britain Covey (knee), and cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring) have also been ruled out.

Tanner McKee, who was benched in favor of Milton this week, is questionable with a rib injury. Cole Payton is the other quarterback on the 53-man roster.

articles.title: The Eagles were trying to hide starting QB change from Giants
articles.summary: Nick Sirianni and the Eagles wanted to keep it a secret that they were benching QB Tanner McKee for Joe Milton.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA — There was confusion around how Nick Sirianni and the Philadelphia Eagles handled their quarterback situation ahead of Sunday's game vs. the New York Giants.

But on Friday, Sirianni cleared things up: he wanted to keep it a secret that the Eagles were going to start Joe Milton instead of Tanner McKee in Week 9.

Let's back it up to how the Eagles — who are stuck in a six-game losing streak, looking for answers — got here.

On Monday, Sirianni said in a video press conference with reporters that McKee was "our guy."

On Tuesday, as we found out on Thursday, McKee was informed that he would no longer be the starting QB.

On Wednesday, Sirianni took the podium at the Jefferson Health Training Complex and didn't announce a QB change.

Less than two hours later, ESPN reported that the Eagles were benching McKee for Milton.

Then, after the Eagles' Wednesday practice, neither McKee nor Milton spoke to reporters in the locker room.

Some players, like Jordan Mailata and Landon Dickerson, tried to spin a a lack of knowledge over who will start at QB. Tight end Dallas Goedert, meanwhile, confirmed that the team was told Milton would start "minutes" before ESPN's report.

Ultimately, Sirianni didn't want that information to get out.

He made that clear in his Friday press conference, the first time he spoke with the media since the Milton news leaked.

"I was going to hold onto that for as long as I possibly could," Sirianni said. "I'm not real shy with you guys. I'm going to tell you guys what I want to tell you guys. I respect the job that y'all have to do. But I'm going to tell you guys what I'm going to tell you guys because I have to protect the team.

"Every second that goes by in a situation like that where you can hold onto information as long as you possibly can is a little less time for the opponent to get ready for the game. And so, I know there's a lot of interest on what you want to hear, what the fans want to hear. My job is to win football games and do everything that we can do to help win football games and protect the guys here on this football team and handle everything we can inside."

Sirianni has withheld information many times in the past to create a "competitive advantage." It's clear that was the plan here, too: to spring Milton on the Giants instead of McKee.

That plan was foiled when ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that McKee, after starting three games, would be benched in favor of Milton, who has been in the building for three weeks.

Milton offers a different skill set to McKee. Milton has mobility, which he can use to escape the constant pressure that has been coming this year behind poor pass protection. McKee, far from a nimble quarterback, was sacked five times vs. the Washington Commander last Sunday.

The Eagles are hoping Milton's mobility and cannon arm can spark what has been an anemic offense.

Sirianni did acknowledge that McKee "played solid" in his three starts. McKee, who was Jalen Hurts' backup last season, completed 72 of 114 passes (63.2%) for 638 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions.

"That's always a difficult thing to think through. Because it isn't ever just on one person," Sirianni said. "But this is just what I felt what we had to do at this particular moment to give us the best chance to win this weekend."

Sirianni said he talked through the QB decision in "great, great detail" with general manager Howie Roseman and his offensive staff. But it was his call as the head coach.

"At the end of the day, I have to make the decision," Sirianni said.

Asked what changed from Monday, when he said McKee was "our guy," to Tuesday, when McKee said he was informed he was benched, Sirianni said: "You think through things. ... As you start to put ideas down, things are fluid."

The QB situation was certainly fluid earlier this week at the Jefferson Health Training Complex.

articles.title: Former Clemson star offensive lineman’s prediction for Clemson vs Syracuse s
articles.summary: Here’s what former Clemson standout offensive lineman Eric Mac Lain is thinking for the Tigers matchup against Syracuse.
articles.body:
Eric Mac Lain expects Clemson to leave Syracuse with a victory Saturday, but his projected margin gives the Tigers little room for error. The former Clemson offensive lineman sees a three-to-six-point game against an Orange team coming off consecutive wins.

Mac Lain and fellow Clemson alum Kelly Gramlich both picked their alma mater on the Gramlich & Mac Lain podcast. Neither sounded particularly comfortable with the matchup, even after the Tigers' road victory over Florida State .

Syracuse has beaten North Carolina and SMU in back-to-back weeks, with the latter coming on a dramatic last-second finish against the then-No. 19 Mustangs. Steve Angeli's return at quarterback has given the Orange offense a boost, adding another challenge for a Clemson team trying to build consistency.

Mac Lain believes the Tigers have the personnel advantage, though he acknowledged that talent alone will not decide the outcome.

"But I think Clemson has figured something out. I hope they continue to build on it, but it is going to be a tough game," he said.

Gramlich shared his pick while expressing even more hesitation.

"I'll take Clemson as well, but I don't feel great about it," she said.

There is enough history between these programs to explain that concern. Syracuse won 34-21 at Clemson last season, and the series has produced several memorable games, including the Orange's 2017 upset and Clemson's Chase Brice-led comeback in 2018.

The Tigers have won three straight trips to Syracuse. Extending that streak Saturday would give Clemson consecutive road victories and another encouraging result entering the final stretch of its season.

articles.title: Eagles legend upset at his former team for pushing Jeff Stoutland out: ‘Don’t give me this crap’
articles.summary: Eagles legend rips Jeff Stoutland narrative.
articles.body:
Former Eagles legend Jason Kelce is upset about the narrative that Eagles players wanted Jeff Stoutland gone after last season.

On Tuesday , 97.5 The Fanatic radio host Bill Colarulo reported that Eagles players wanted a new offensive line coach to lead the room. They wanted a new voice.

So, after 13 seasons, Stoutland left the Eagles' organization in February.

"That one very much upset me," Kelce said on the 94WIP morning show about the Stoutland report. "Because the reason to move off of Jeff Stoutland had nothing to do with the players. Had to do with the building wanting to go in a different direction. That's fine, but don't give me this crap, trying to defer direction on the decisions you guys wanted to make."

Kelce is upset that certain members of the Eagles' organization are not willing to stand behind their statements. They are hiding behind a report.

"The leaks coming out and the unnamed sources," Kelce said about what bothers him. "It really bothers me because as a player. And the reason I'm telling people listening, I would take anything you hear from an unnamed source with a giant grain of salt. Because ultimately that person isn't willing to stand behind it in front of a camera, and usually that unnamed source has some type of incentive or reason that they're putting this out to a media member. And it's usually to cover their own behind."

articles.title: Relationship between Paige and Azzi has been over for a year, but they’re still friends, Bueckers says
articles.summary: Former UConn women’s basketball teammates Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd addressed their relationship Friday on a podcast, saying it had been over for over a y...
articles.body:
Former UConn women's basketball teammates Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd addressed their relationship Friday on a podcast, saying it had been over for over a year.

On Fudd's "Fudd Around And Find Out" podcast, Buecker said of her current Dallas Wings teammate, "We're not together anymore; it's been a while. (We) share that because everybody [was] like, 'Oh my gosh, they're teammates, how is this going to work?'"

Fudd was drafted No. 1 by the Wings on April 13 but Bueckers said the relationship was already over at that point.

"She was not drafted because she was my girlfriend," Bueckers said on the podcast. "She was drafted because she deserved it. She's an amazing human, an amazing basketball player. And we're still friends, we're still cool.

"We played an entire season together; we're the utmost professionals."

The issue was brought up at Fudd's initial Wings press conference when Dallas Morning News reporter Kevin Sherrington asked about their relationship status and how they planned to balance that dynamic playing with each other but Sherrod was rebuked by a Wings' public relations representative and Fudd did not answer the question. The moment was widely shared on social media, with some saying their relationship was personal and private and others saying that it was a legitimate question because it could affect the team dynamic.

Their relationship became public in the summer of 2025 after the Huskies won the national championship.

Fudd played only 30 games this WNBA season due to a right knee injury. She had arthroscopic surgery in August.

"My off-season's been good," Fudd said on the podcast. "Lots of rehab, lots of training, lots of on-court workouts, lots of traveling. It's been busy."

Fudd will be at UConn Sunday to be inducted into the Huskies of Honor before UConn's game against Iowa at M&T Arena at Gampel Pavilion. The ceremony will take place at 1:30 p.m. and the game will tip off at 2 p.m.

articles.title: After controversial penalty, Moledo reveals threats against his family

Coritiba defender Moledo was the central figure in last Tuesday's (3) clash between Internacional and Coxa after conceding a stoppage-time penalty to his former club.

The foul led to Alerrandro's goal, which secured victory for a still-desperate Colorado and kept the Paraná side firmly on alert in the battle against relegation.

The Coritiba defender had not spoken publicly since the match in Porto Alegre.

That changed this Friday (6), when he posted a story on his Instagram profile.

He said he had made the "wrong decision" when he caught Juninho.

He also revealed that his family had received threats on social media.

According to journalist Rogerio Scarione, Moledo cried uncontrollably after the match in Porto Alegre. He even needed to be comforted by his teammates.

articles.body:
After the Portland Blazers parted ways with head coach Tiago Splitter in favor of Micah Nori, many wondered how it would affect the team's young players, including fourth-year guard Scoot Henderson . Coach Nori's unique approach to his first year with the Blazers included instructing his coaching staff to read "The Old Man and the Sea," by Ernest Hemingway.

For the players, it's Nori's attention to detail that stands out most, Henderson said, per The Athletic's Jason Quick.

"We lacked small details," Henderson said. "Great teams are big on that, from what I can see, just playing against them. Going back to last year, we lacked some of the small details. Nori is helping us with that."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Scoot Henderson and the Blazers have the best record (6-1) in the Western Conference standings. Two weeks into the regular season, head coach Micah Nori has his team fully committed to success, led by All-Star Deni Avdija and veterans Damian Lillard, Ja Morant, and Jrue Holiday.

"I'm getting way too much credit, I really am; I'm not just saying that," Nori said. "I'm not trying to be overly humble, but I'm getting way too much credit for putting really good players in good positions. It's playing to their strengths; that's all."

Portland is leading the league in scoring (121.9). Last year, the Blazers averaged the most turnovers in the NBA, more than 17 a game. This season, they rank 14th out of 30, averaging nearly two fewer. The vast improvements, along with early returns this season, have them positioned to become one of the better teams in the association.

articles.title: Diamondbacks' Corbin Carroll discusses his elbow surgery | Exclusive
articles.summary: Arizona Diamondbacks star Corbin Carroll had arthroscopic surgery on his right elbow. He spoke with The Republic about it.
articles.body:
Diamondbacks right fielder Corbin Carroll underwent surgery on Thursday, Nov. 5, to remove loose bodies in his right elbow, a minor procedure that he hopes will set back his offseason work by less than a month.

Carroll said he felt "a little bit" of discomfort in the elbow during the season but that the discomfort worsened last week.

"I'm guessing a couple broke off during the season and a couple broke off last week," Carroll told The Arizona Republic Friday, Nov. 6. "Last week was when I really had significant symptoms where it was like, 'Hey this is worth taking a look.'"

He said he had the minimally invasive NanoScope procedure, the same one then-Detroit Tigers left-hander Tarik Skubal had during this past season that allowed him to return from the injured list in only six weeks.

"I'm hoping to start swinging the bat at the beginning of December," Carroll said.

The Arizona Battlebacks? Photos from Diamondbacks' comeback wins in 2026

Earlier this week, Carroll won his first Gold Glove Award after being named a finalist for the second year in a row. He was one of three Diamondbacks to win a Gold Glove this year.

"I think it's rewarding to a lot of the work that I've put in with (outfield coach Dave) McKay," Carroll said. "It's just going to be cool to be able to give McKay something like that as a thank you for all the extra swings that he put in for me and all the extra time."

Carroll typically shagged fly balls with McKay twice a series before games.

Though the right elbow needed the surgery, the bigger issue for Carroll this season was his back, an area he said has been a focus for him over the past month. He said he is trying to get himself in good positions in the weight room in hopes of avoiding similar back problems in the future.

He equated the severity of this week's surgery to the hamate procedure he had at the start of spring training.

"It's the removal of something as opposed to fixing something," he said. "I would say in terms of the pain and all that, so far it's been less than the hamate."

Carroll, 26, is coming off a season in which he hit .239/.328/.467 with 22 homers, 33 doubles and 17 triples.

He said he had not yet begun to make any offseason adjustments with his swing. He had been planning to start hitting in the middle of November but will have to push that back two weeks.

articles.title: Everton 2-1 Coventry City: Live | Barry’s rapid brace

articles.body:
69' – Branthwaite steps up and fires a low cross into the box, but it's too close to Rushworth and Barry can't get to it.

66' – KDH stings Rushworth's palms with a shot, but George was offside on that.

65' – Brave from Rohl to take on Awoniyi in the box for a cross, and Everton can break through Garner.

61' – GOALLLL!! Another cross into the box and Barry and Rushworth get into a tangle, and inadvertently or not Barry gets a touch that pushes the ball over the line, and just like that Everton lead 2-1!! BARRY HAS SCORED AGAIN!!

58' – Everton are keeping the pressure on the visitors, hemming them into their own half.

57' – Dibling with a great run, cross into the box, headed back across but Coventry clear. Not too far, and Myko crosses again, half-cleared again. Garner finds the left back again and he delivers a peach of a cross onto the six-yard line and BARRY SCORES! He met the ball perfectly and Rushworth got a hand to it but could not keep it out, 1-1!

55' – Visitors attack again and now Gboho's touch sees the ball go off Armstrong's arm, but ref immediately says no penalty, phew.

53' – FIVE Everton defenders around Gboho and no one can get the ball away from the Coventry player and he pokes it past Pickford for the visitors to lead the game 1-0. Farcical football from Everton.

49' – KDH to Rohl, and he slides Armstrong in and the midfielder tries a shot on the run, but not good contact and the goalie gathers easily. Coventry are gaining in confidence here as they play out from the back right through the middle of the park, ball goes out to the right and cross back into the box was too high.

48' – Awoniyi gets in ahead of Myko and as the pair rush towards the box the striker puts his leg in front of the defender before going down in a heap. Ref says no penalty and VAR concurs that contact was outside the box. Sneaky bugger that Taiwo lad.

46' – Coventry get the second half underway, no changes from either side. Poor touch allows the visitors to run at the defence, Gboho shot deflected but straight to Pickford.

Halftime Thoughts – Everton did not make their good start count and have allowed Coventry to get set and impose themselves here. Will Moyes rely on giving the boys a stern talking-to, or will he actually make some changes?

45+1' – Coventry with another long throw that Garner can block and there's the halftime whistle. Everton started well but have been outplayed for the last twenty or so minutes.

45' – Finally an Everton attack but Rohl's cross is poor and goes out. One minute to be added on here.

44' – Coventry cross into the box, and a visitor's player goes down next to Tarky. VAR review says no foul, looks like it was Tarky being investigated for a hair pull?

43' – Long throw knocked on by Pinnock, Everton marshal them away, but with Dibling and Dasilva dueling for the ball, the call goes against the Everton player and the fans are unhappy. Torp lines up the freekick from well over thirty yards out, and it's straight at Pickford and he two-fists it away.

41' – Myko turns into trouble and again Coventry can attack. Ball comes to Rudoni and he fires off a shot at the far post, Pickford stretches and it's just wide.

37' – Long throw causes chaos in the Everton box, Pinnock gets to it and cannot shoot, then it comes to Rudoni with his back to goal and he tries to get fancy and Everton can clear. The home fans are deeply displeased what has gone on in the last few minutes.

35' – Coventry attack through the middle before they have space on the Everton left, and George slides in with a big block to cut out a cross, corner. Into the mess in the box, Pickford punches away, ball back into the six-yard box and Tarky with a big block. Rudoni finds Sakamoto in space and he can shoot, Pickford parries it away, whew.

33' – Branthwaite charges forward and wants the ball, Armstrong dallies on it and is caught out and Coventry have a chance to create an odd-man rush, but Dibling leads the blue rush back and can clear the danger.

32' – Gboho and Torp have both had cracks from far out, and they've been far off too. Everton had a chance at a counter but KDH's pass seeking Barry is poor.

30' – Another Coventry cross, headed away by Myko, George can't clear it. Myko gets in front of the next cross, balloons up into the air and Pickford takes it.

28' – Coventry probe the Everton left but Myko and George do enough to hold them off. Now Rohl can cross from the left after Dibling gets in front of a bouncing ball, but it's overhit and races away for a goalkick.

24' – Another good spell here as Everton hold the ball on the left, exhaust all possibilities, circulate it back to the right, before Dibling finds Barry in a spot where he could turn, but instead of trying a shot he lofts a cross into the six-yard box with no blue shirts anywhere.

21' – Rohl and Dibling cannot prevent a cross coming into the box, but Rudoni's header is poor and wide, and Everton are lucky. Dibling does well to get the ball back from a pair of Coventry players by the touchline, and is fouled.

17' – Everton corner now from the left. Taken short, Garner swings it into the back post but it's too high even for the giant Branthwaite.

12' – Delightful diagonal from Garner almost finds Dibling in acres of space behind the backline but the first time league starter cannot control it. Mfuni fouls George and Everton have a freekick midway between the box and the center circle. KDH puts it into the box, the ball pings around and Armstrong has two clean looks at goal and still cannot get it in the net! Oh nevermind, Thierno Barry had handled the ball anyway.

9' – 18-yr-old Mfuni does well to stop KDH on a break. Now another counter and Tyrique George gets it to Barry on the right, and he dallies on it, and dallies on it and his shot is blocked. Da Silva doesn't clear and it comes to Vitaliy Mykolenko but his shot is straightforward and Rushworth punches his attempt away.

8' – A hopeful cross into the ball is just over Awoniyi's head and skids past Jordan Pickford's left post, and the goalie makes a nervous late dive to ensure it's going wide.

5' – Rushworth with an awful clearance but the goalie is lucky as Garner cuts out the pass but Everton cannot turn it into a shot.

3' – Awoniyi gets to a long ball in between Jarrad Branthwaite and James Tarkowski, but Garner is quick to clear. The long-throw into the box is hoofed away.

1'- James Garner gets us underway, Everton in a blue-white-blue combination, Coventry are white-peach-white. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall gets the ball and is met by boos from the away contingent, given his history as a Leicester City player.

The players are walking out to Z-Cars with the captains of both sides holding poppy wreaths which are part of the Remembrance Day commemoration events being held by all clubs. The bugle final farewell is met by a loud roar of appreciate, and we're ready to play some football.

With the latter, Marchenko went down with a lower-body injury on October 26 during a game in Calgary against the Flames. articles.title: Yankees Mailbag: An early look at outfield options
articles.summary: The Yankees could use an outfielder if they want to have the best unit in baseball, but is there a clean fit?
articles.body:
Good afternoon everyone, it's time to dive back into the mailbag and answer some of your questions. Remember to send in your questions for our bi-weekly call by e-mail to pinstripealleyblog [at] gmail [dot] com .

Darth_Lazarus asks: If the CBA negotiations go really sideways is there a possibility we see replacement player games next year?

Never say never, but I doubt the owners would want to go this route even if it's looking like the season is completely lost. Recruiting scab players at this point in the league's history would be a black eye on ownership and would completely kill any goodwill they could have with the public as these negotiations drag on, as the product on the field will be a clearly inferior copy that wouldn't draw much interest while also making them look desperate to recoup on the broadcast deals they've negotiated. Speaking of those broadcasting rights, while the league is a much more regional product than the NFL or NBA and several teams were having trouble finding an actual partner for their TV audience, it's my hope that the prospect of future negotiations with broadcasters is one of the pressure points pushing ownership to get to the table sooner rather than later resulting in an actual season being played out in 2027 — perhaps a bit too hopeful, considering the lines in the sand that have been drawn this time around, but a girl can dream.

LocalBlueWhaleRuinsEverything asks: With the Yankees needing some offense, could they consider Arozarena or Suzuki? Theoretically, they could stick one in LF and have Cody move to CF. It's not something I'd want them to do long term, but for one season I'd be interested. Stanton and Garcia should be gone after next season, so in the future you'd a spare DH spot to rotate them.

Theoretically they could, but that takes a lot of the value that Bellinger provides away by moving his excellent left field defense over to center field, where he has been underwhelming at best since 2021. Arozarena and Suzuki are both quality offensive options that would improve the lineup tremendously, but the defensive setback that adding either would cause problems down the line. That being said, the free agent market for true center fielders is abysmal, so if they're looking for an upgrade they're going to have to get creative with trades to find it.

Johnny1944 asks: It seems JD was overhyped for years by Cash. Does he have any real value?

Jasson Domínguez's career is looking like a relatively unremarkable one, which is what tends to happen to the majority of MLB players — but most players don't get compared to Mickey Mantle when they were 17 years old. That unfair expectation has felt like a weight on Domínguez's shoulders the entire time that he's been in the organization, with every glimpse of a solid run down in the minors being heralded as the turning point where he was going to spark a path straight to the majors. However, Domínguez has now had two full seasons in proximity to the majors, and while he's still very young entering his age-24 season in 2027 it just doesn't seem like there's much to work with in his game.

Our own Andrés tackled the idea of whether the Yankees should move on from Domínguez the other day, and while his conclusion was that there's no pressure to do so immediately time is running out for the former wonder prospect. He's got one minor league option remaining meaning he's likely to start the year in the minors, and while there's some underlying promise in his peripherals the majority of his Savant page is disappointing. Domínguez's defense has been atrocious to watch, and he's alternated from being unable to hit lefties to being unable to hit righties. If there was just some consistency to his game he'd at least be able to stick around as a bench option in the majors, but as is he's got to get consistent playing time to try and make something of himself and he isn't going to find that in pinstripes at the moment.

OLDY MOLDY asks: How reliable are Cole, Fried, and Rodón next year considering recent arm problems in the last 3 seasons and age? Any innings projections? Does Schlittler come back to earth in 2027?

I don't have many concerns about Max Fried at the moment — he'll probably be good for one short-term IL stint but otherwise give the team 25-30 starts and has been lights out when he has been active. Likewise, while Gerrit Cole has missed significant time over the past couple of seasons the core issue has now been dealt with and he should be fully healthy entering 2027. It's wild to think that we're already seven years into the nine-year deal that Cole signed with the team, but there's just two seasons left of his contract and if you told me back then that he'd have compiled three top five Cy Young finishes with one win up to this point, I'd be pretty content entering the final days of that deal. Carlos Rodón has salvaged his Yankees career quite well following his disastrous first year in pinstripes, but of the three his health still concerns me more going forward — not enough to panic, but enough to keep my eye on how he's getting through each start even when he's on. As for Cam Schlittler, the sky is the ceiling for the team's newfound ace and while it would certainly be unrealistic to expect a 1.95 ERA as the standard going forward I think he'll remain the team's best pitcher next year as he comes into his own.

articles.title: Rey Mysterio Reveals Survivor Series Match, WWE Rumors on Cruz Montana and Michael Chandler

articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Rey Mysterio Announces 5-on-5 Survivor Series Match

What Cruz Montana Debut Says About NXT 🤔

WWE Hall of Famer and AAA general manager Rey Mysterio revealed Friday that a unique match will be part of the Survivor Series card in Houston on Nov. 28.

Appearing on What's Your Story? With Stephanie McMahon (h/t WrestlePurists ), Mysterio announced that the traditional, five-on-five elimination match concept is returning for Survivor Series 2026:

Mysterio noted that he spoke with Raw general manager Adam Pearce and SmackDown general manager Nick Aldis, and they came to an agreement to hold a Team USA vs. Team Mexico five-on-five elimination bout at Survivor Series.

The match participants have yet to be announced, but it seems likely that Penta, Rey Fenix and Dragon Lee will be part of Team Mexico given how heavily they have been featured on WWE programming in recent weeks and months.

Since 2022, Survivor Series has been paired with the WarGames tagline, and every Survivor Series over that stretch has been headlined by WarGames matches.

An unfortunate side effect of WarGames has been the extinction of the traditional elimination match, which is the foundation Survivor Series was built upon.

In 1987, Survivor Series became WWE's second annual pay-per-view event, following in the footsteps of WrestleMania.

Five-on-five elimination matches made up the entirety of Survivor Series for many years, and they continued to be part of the show for decades, even as other types of matches were added.

A full Survivor Series card of only five-on-five elimination matches may never come to fruition again, but keeping the tradition alive by having at least one such match is something that figures to appeal to current and old-school fans alike.

Reported Details on Montana's Main Roster Call-Up

Cruz Montana shocked the WWE Universe during Monday night's episode of Raw by attacking Bloodline leader Roman Reigns and joining 946.

According to Dave Meltzer of the Wrestling Observer Newsletter (h/t Felix Upton of Ringside News), Montana joining 946 was a "late decision," and "nobody in NXT was aware of it" ahead of time.

Meltzer did not indicate if those not in the know included NXT head Shawn Michaels, but he did note that Michaels "absolutely had plans going forward with Montana as a top babyface" before his call-up.

A match between Royce Keys and Solo Sikoa was ruled a no-contest when 946 members interfered, leading to The Bloodline backing up Sikoa and brawling 946.

In the midst of the chaos, a masked man took out Reigns, and he revealed himself to be Montana.

It was an unexpected moment since Montana had only recently debuted in NXT and was among the brand's top babyfaces, feuding with DarkState's Dion Lennox.

On Wednesday night's episode of NXT, two days after his main roster debut, Montana worked a match as a babyface against Lennox, and 946 also got a face reaction when it showed up to even the odds against DarkState.

Montana will be a heel going forward on the main roster, though, and all signs point toward him being part of 946's team in a likely WarGames match against The Bloodline at Survivor Series later this month.

Chandler Reportedly Considered for Future WWE Match

UFC star Michael Chandler reportedly could be considered for additional WWE appearances and even a match in the future.

On Wednesday's episode of NXT, Chandler served as the special guest referee for the Cruz Montana vs. Dion Lennox unsanctioned match since NXT general manager Robert Stone wanted someone who could keep things in order.

According to False Finish , there have been "discussions" about Chandler having a WWE match at some point.

Chandler's WWE involvement has been rumored for quite some time, as False Finish previously reported in August that he was spotted at the WWE Performance Center.

The 40-year-old Chandler was a three-time Bellator lightweight champion, and he later became a contender for the UFC lightweight title.

While Chandler is technically still an active fighter, he has lost each of his past four fights and six of his last seven.

That suggests it could be time for Chandler to explore other opportunities, and given his combat sports background and big personality, a foray into WWE would make a lot of sense.

articles.title: Will 97 Catch 99 This Season? Wayne Gretzky on Connor McDavid's Chase of History
articles.summary: TORONTO - Connor McDavid is up to 44 points through 17 games after a four-point performance in the Oilers' game against the Ducks on Thursday night.
articles.body:
TORONTO - Connor McDavid is up to 44 points through 17 games after a four-point performance in the Oilers' game against the Ducks on Thursday night.

He has more assists (34) than any other player has points, and he's currently on pace for 217 points over an 84-game schedule, which would set a new NHL single-season record.

That would break the single-season points record that none other than Wayne Gretzky set. His 215 points in 80 games in 1985-86 with the Oilers still stand as the single-season record.

Records are meant to be broken, and we never thought we'd see anyone get close to Gretzky's all-time goals-scored record of 894 before Alex Ovechkin broke it in 2025 . But if anyone is going to achieve the mark, it would be McDavid.

But what's more impressive to Gretzky than the points being put up by McDavid this season is the way he's leading the Oilers this season after being bounced last postseason by the Ducks.

"More importantly [than his record-setting pace, McDavid is] a wonderful young man, and what he's doing for his hockey team, for the game, for the city of Edmonton — it's unmatched right now," Gretzky said to the media at an event commemorating a legacy partnership with trading card company Upper Deck .

In collaboration with the Hockey Hall of Fame, Upper Deck and Gretzky also revealed the 'Walter Gretzky Upper Deck Hockey Resource Centre,' an archival tribute to Gretzky's late father and his influence on his career.

The Oilers have gotten off to a red-hot 11-3-3 start, leading the Pacific Division and McDavid would be a first-ballot Hall of Famer if his career ended today.

But like McDavid, though, Gretzky's primary concern was less about individual accolades and more about winning. While Gretzky led the Oilers to four Cups and McDavid is still seeking his first, Gretzky spoke with high praise and confidence for McDavid in this respect on Friday.

"He's on a mission to win a Stanley Cup; he wants it desperately, and that's what you need out of your best player and your captain," Gretzky said. "You need that leadership that you want to get to that next level, and he has that in him."

Let's remind you, dear reader, that this isn't just anyone saying this about McDavid. This is hockey's GOAT, the Great One himself.

Gretzky just sees this as the natural evolution of sports, where players can seemingly do things that seemed impossible in the past.

"It's incredible," Gretzky said. "[McDavid] is a tremendous young man; he's obviously a great hockey player, and what he's doing is truly remarkable. "Today, the athletes, and I say this with a great deal of respect, as time goes on, the equipment gets better, the athletes get bigger and better, the game gets better, and it's all positive. And what he's doing now is remarkable."

articles.title: BOBBY BURACK: Ryan Clark claims ESPN interviewed Sophie Cunningham about trans athletes to impress OutKick
articles.summary: Ryan Clark claims ESPN published a Sophie Cunningham profile about trans athletes in women's sports to impress OutKick after his firing from ESPN.
articles.body: Former ESPN employee Ryan Clark claims the company published a profile featuring Sophie Cunningham’s comments about trans athletes after his firing to impress OutKick. ESPN fired Clark more than three months ago, yet he still discusses his ousting on a regular basis. The New York Post summarized his appearance on the "All The Smoke" podcast Thursday. "Sophie Cunningham says something and they [OutKick] say, ‘A great brand switch for ESPN. Ryan Clark was fired this week and now Sophie Cunningham leads the news,’" Clark said before alleging that ESPN leaked news of his firing to OutKick. "That’s what they [ESPN] wanted. That’s why you leaked it to [OutKick]. And so I think everything points to it, but I should have, my antenna should have been up more and even with that, there was nothing I could change." CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Clark first accused ESPN of coordinating with OutKick to "humiliate" him three days after his firing. However, as we have documented on multiple occasions, that is not accurate. In short, OutKick learned that Clark was among several employees ESPN planned to lay off as part of its budget cuts. We informed the network that we were going to report the news because Clark was the most notable name on the list. (We also reported Cam Newton’s ousting when we learned of that news the next day). Amid an email exchange with ESPN PR about our reporting, an executive informed Clark during a commercial break on "NFL Live" that he would be laid off. He did not return for the next segment. Our understanding is that the company fired Clark during the show because it feared we would not hold the information until after the broadcast. ESPN management did not want Clark to learn about the decision online. ESPN did not "humiliate" Clark on purpose. It tried to protect him. The decision, however, backfired — badly. Had ESPN told us that Clark was unaware and asked us to hold the news until he knew, we would have. Further, ESPN did not leak the news to us. My colleague Dan Zaksheske and I had four independent sources. In fact, ESPN tried to prevent us from breaking it. The profile generated headlines and protests outside WNBA games because Cunningham voiced support for keeping trans athletes out of girls’ sports. "I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I’m like, ‘I never once said that.’ I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men," Cunningham told ESPN. Damn her for extending love while wanting to keep little girls safe! Clark claimed ESPN profiled Cunningham to show OutKick that it had completed a "brand switch." Not quite. ESPN fired him more than three months ago. He has continued to blame everyone but himself for the decision. He has blamed his former bosses, OutKick, Clay Travis, Dan Zaksheske, me and the "culture change." In reality, none of us are to blame. Ryan Clark is to blame. He got himself fired. ESPN fired him because he was toxic. He made false statements about the role Louisiana police allegedly played in the death of former LSU Tigers wide receiver Kyren Lacy. He shamed Robert Griffin III for marrying a white woman. He race-baited by trade. He undermined and disrespected Peter Schrager on air. He shouted the F-word at Schrager off air afterward. articles.title: WWE SmackDown Winners, Live Grades, Reaction and Highlights Before Crown Jewel 2026
articles.summary: We're less than 24 hours from Crown Jewel, but WWE had one last stop to make for this week's SmackDown.
articles.body:
We're less than 24 hours from Crown Jewel, but WWE had one last stop to make for this week's SmackDown.

CM Punk and Kevin Owens met in a No Disqualification match this week, which was heightened by KO costing Punk the NXT title on Tuesday when he challenged Grayson Waller.

We also saw the women's tag titles on the line when B-Fab and Michin defended the belts against Lainey Reid and Fallon Henley.

Let's take a look at everything that happened on the final SmackDown before Crown Jewel.

Will You Ride or Die with the Last Real Good Guy

Sami Zayn showed up to talk about his upcoming match against Roman Reigns, but Jimmy Uso came out to confront him.

They drew from their history and referenced several moments to tell the story they were trying to tell, and it worked. This felt like a personal argument more than a wrestling promo.

Big Jim said Zayn used 946 attacking The Bloodline on Monday to his advantage, which means he is no longer family.

Moments later, 946 showed up and attacked Jimmy as Zayn watched from the apron without helping. He did not look happy to see Jim in that situation, but he did nothing to help.

This was a good segment. Using their real history helped make it feel deeper, and the image of Zayn walking away as Jimmy was assaulted was unexpected.

Last time in action: MFTs defeated Bakusai (SD, October 22)

Shinsuke Nakamura and Tama Tonga finally met for a singles match this week, and they wasted no time upping the intensity.

They skipped the lockup and grappling and went right to throwing punches and kicks. Neither man wanted to relent, even when the ref tried to separate them.

Talla Tonga interfered behind the ref's back with a big boot to Nakamura's face as the show cut to a break.

They had about 10 minutes to work, so while they weren't able to make this a marathon, they did manage to make it into an entertaining sprint. It was a pretty simple match overall, but it pushed their feud forward.

Even though Tama had Talla and Haku at ringside for help, he was unable to overcome the former NXT champion. Nakamura pulled off the victory, which might lead to a tag title rematch down the line.

Having Haku around again is fun, but WWE needs to find interesting ways to use him. He's an interesting guy who can add a lot.

It was nice to see Tama have a chance to return to his old style of intense offense after spending so long in tag matches having to hold back.

The way Tama rolls someone into a suplex looks cool.

An angry Gunther came to the ring to talk about what happened last Friday with Danhausen and Finn Bálor, who returned as The Demon.

He said every word he has ever said about Bálor is true, and that his career is hanging on by a thread. Gunther said Balor should just end his career tonight to get it over with.

The Ring General looked into the camera and addressed Finn directly. He said he used to respect Balor, and he wants him to come face him like a man without the makeup and theatrics. It took Bálor almost no time to show up.

After talking for a minute, Finn tried to attack Gunther. The Ring General almost took another Coup de Grace, but he thwarted it. Bálor avoided the powerbomb and climbed back up, but Gunther rolled out of the ring to avoid his finisher.

This was all very cut and dry. It was a simple and easy segment to continue the feud that started last week. Nothing special happened, but it's early in the story. They have plenty of time to ramp things up.

Having Punk continuously body-shame Owens in promos and interviews makes it hard to see him as a good guy in all of this.

Casual Gunther is less intimidating. He needs to get back to the suits and track suits.

Jacy Jayne getting Byron Saxton's name wrong is such a classic heel way to be a jerk, but she made it feel natural in her backstage segment.

Last time in action: Fatal Influence lost to Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley (SD, October 9), B-Fab and Michin defeated Bliss and Paxley (SD, October 23)

The women's tag titles were on the line this week when B-Fab and Michin defended the belts against former champions Henley and Reid.

This match only lasted about three and a half minutes. They tried to pack as much in as they could, but with so little time, it wasn't easy.

The length made it feel like a match from the Divas era, which is not a compliment. Henley and Michin definitely stood out as looking the best with their offense, but they barely had enough time to make an impact.

Paxley and Bliss attacked Jayne and Cargill from the crowd before going into the ring and causing the match to end prematurely. Bayley and Charlotte Flair also came out to join the fight.

Having so many people fighting at the end was kind of fun, but the actual match that was scheduled was a letdown.

Jayne and Jade Cargill not having more of a feud over the U.S. title feels like a missed opportunity to have two feuds in one with these groups.

articles.title: Cowboys WR George Pickens questionable for game vs. Colts
articles.summary: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer shared an encouraging George Pickens injury update ahead of Sunday's Week 9 matchup with the Indianapolis Colts.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts could be facing the Dallas Cowboys at close to full strength at wide receiver on Sunday, Nov. 8.

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer provided an update Friday regarding star receiver George Pickens, who has been hampered by a hamstring injury prior to the Week 9 matchup.

During an appearance on 105.3 The Fan , Schottenheimer indicated that Dallas is hopeful Pickens will be available against Indianapolis.

The receiver was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday because of the hamstring issue. He is officially listed as questionable for Sunday's game.

Pickens has continued playing through injuries in recent weeks, despite his offensive involvement declining.

The 25-year-old caught just two passes for 48 yards on four targets during Dallas' 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals in Week 8.

His reduced playing time has also generated doubts about the Cowboys' offensive approach.

However, offensive coordinator Klayton Adams explained Thursday that Pickens' limited workload has been injury-related rather than a reflection of his performance.

"There's been a couple of weeks now where George has been banged up, and we've limited him in some capacities because of that," Adams said, according to Dallas Sports Journal .

Pickens' availability could be huge for an Indianapolis defense aiming to rebound from a rough stretch.

The Colts surrendered 42 points in their Week 8 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars and will now prep to defend a Dallas passing attack featuring Pickens and fellow standout receiver CeeDee Lamb.

Indianapolis and Dallas will kick off Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at Lucas Oil Stadium, with the game airing on FOX.

articles.title: 'Two-headed monster' on point for Hope College women's basketball this season
articles.summary: Terin Maynard and Josie DeSmit lead the Flying Dutch into a reloading season.
articles.body:
Hope women’s basketball takes on UW-Platteville in the season opener

HOLLAND - The Hope College women's basketball team has been a national powerhouse for decades.

Designed to win with defense, this year's version of the Flying Dutch has two experienced point guards leading the way on both sides of the ball.

Starting point guard Terin Maynard pushes the pace, drives to the basket and anchors the perimeter defense.

While most teams lose quite a bit when a backup point guard goes in.

For Hope, there is hardly a noticeable difference when Josie DeSmit checks in.

The duo led Hope to a 72-65 win over Wisconsin-Platteville on Friday, Nov. 6, at DeVos Fieldhouse to open the season - both scoring career highs in the process.

Maynard scored a career-high 20 points to go along with six assists, while DeSmit had a career-high 15 points with three steals. Leah Richards had 15 points and eight rebounds.

"They were really good today," Hope coach Brian Morehouse said. "Josie is good enough to start and played her role very well. It gives us a two-headed monster and that is really hard on other teams."

The game was close in the fourth quarter and Morehouse chose to play both point guards together. DeSmit nailed a 3-pointer, then scored another basket to make it 64-54 with 4:50 to go.

"We showed our resilience and found a way to stick together and do the dirty work," Maynard said.

The Pioneers closed the gap again and Maynard took over with three-point play and a basket in the paint to make it 71-63 with 2:26 to go.

"We withstood 11 from 3 and gutted it out. We switched our defenses up and our defense was really good, but they had a lot of good shots in the last seconds of the shot clock. We played both of them together and if they can rebound a little more we will see that some more."

"We push each other every day in practice. I get to go up against the best defender in the MIAA. We feed off each other well and have some good chemistry," DeSmit said. "We both have our own strengths. Those differences help a ton on the court."

This is the second year they have been the top two point guards on the roster.

"It has been awesome to have her. When we do both go out there, we have the confidence in each other and can read each other," Maynard said. "We found a way to do that well."

It could key another strong season for the Flying Dutch.

"We have a lot of potential this year," Maynard said. "We have great new freshman who have grown our circle and we are starting better than we finished last year. We can only go up."

articles.title: After a 75-Yard Touchdown, Can Stanford Find More Ways to Use Aiden Black?
articles.summary: After a stunning 75-yard touchdown debut, the Cardinal must decide if the physical tight end is a secret weapon ready to ignite an explosive, multidimensiona...
articles.body:
Stanford football's trip to Louisville ended in a 52-24 loss , and most of what happened was easy to forget. One play, however, stood out.

Tight end Aiden Black caught his only target of the game for 75 yards and a touchdown. It was the first reception, receiving yards and touchdown of his college career. The question now is whether Stanford will treat it as a one-off or find ways to build on it.

Black is not a stranger to the program, although he has played a relatively quiet role. The 6-foot-4, 245-pound tight end from Dingmans Ferry, Pennsylvania, earned a spot on the All-ACC Academic Team in 2025 and appeared in all 12 games that season, primarily on special teams.

His high school production suggests he has the ability to contribute as a receiver. At Delaware Valley, Black recorded 75 receptions for 1,307 yards and 15 touchdowns, averaging 17.4 yards per catch. He was also considered the consensus top tight end in Pennsylvania, with ESPN ranking him as high as No. 31 nationally at the position.

His usage in 2026, however, has been extremely limited. Black has received just three targets all season and has the one reception. His 75-yards-per-catch average comes from a very small sample, and one big play does not establish a consistent role. Still, it gives Stanford a reason to explore what he could offer in the passing game.

The timing is particularly important for a Stanford offense that needs more reliable ways to generate explosive plays. The Cardinal scored 24 points against Louisville, more than they had combined in their first three road games (17). Despite the improvement, they still lost by 28 points. The offense showed signs of life, but it needs additional contributors alongside Caden High and Nico Brown.

There are several ways Stanford could incorporate Black without making major changes to its offensive approach. Play-action concepts could draw linebackers toward Micah Ford and create openings for Black in the middle of the field. His size also makes him an option near the goal line, while his receiving background could give Davis Warren another target on third downs.

These possibilities would not require Black to become a featured player immediately. Even a few additional targets could force opposing defenses to account for another receiving threat. His blocking ability will also remain important in determining how frequently he can stay on the field, and that's an area where he has struggled most of the season.

Black's run blocking has received a 58.8 run block grade from PFF, while his pass blocking has been much better at a 68.5. Of course, these opportunities have also come in a small sample, with 87 snaps in run blocking and just 23 in pass blocking.

Stanford has a bye on Nov. 7 before traveling to face Virginia Tech on Nov. 14. The extra preparation time gives Tavita Pritchard's staff an opportunity to evaluate Black's role following his breakout performance.

articles.title: Broncos Roster Move Spells Excellent Sign for Talanoa Hufanga
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos releasing safety Taylor Rapp likely means that starter Talanoa Hufanga is likely returning to the field in Week 9. The post Broncos Roster...
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos made what some consider to be a surprise move when they released safety Taylor Rapp on Friday.

Despite starting the season on the practice squad, Rapp played a starting role on defense over the past three weeks, and prior to his third start in Week 8, was elevated to the active roster.

Now no longer having need of the 28-year old's services implies that safety Talanoa Hufanga; who did not practice on Wednesday and was limited on Thursday; is good to go for Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers.

Taylor Rapp Cut; Suggests Talanoa Hufanga Will Play Week 9

The former Buffalo Bill had been covering Hufanga's duties whilst the two-time All-Pro safety dealt with an ankle injury over the past few weeks, alongside fellow starter Brandon Jones .

Officially, Hufanga is "questionable", but the timing of the announcement feels inescapable; the Broncos surely would not release their interim starter for the past three weeks without a high degree of confidence that their top guy was ready to go.

Especially given the two next men up, Devon Key and Tycen Anderson , have four combined NFL starts between them.

Even then, two of Key's starts were in Week 6 and Week 7, during which he played less than 40% of snaps on defense, with Rapp and Jones seeing the majority of the action.

Anderson himself is mostly a special teams contributor, so if Hufanga is not ready, then the Broncos will have no full-time safety option behind Jones and Key.

articles.title: Former Dodgers Hitting Coach Aaron Bates Explains Why He Left
articles.summary: Former Los Angeles Dodgers hitting coach Aaron Bates opened up about the behind-the-scenes details of his departure.
articles.body:
Former Los Angeles Dodgers hitting coach Aaron Bates opened up about the behind-the-scenes details of his departure.

How Aaron Bates and the Dodgers parted ways

According to Bates, he received a multi-year offer, which he told Maddie Lee of the LA Times was "not a competitive offer."

He rejected the offer and expected talks to continue, but no other follow-up offer came.

"Basically, they said, 'I think we should go our separate ways," Bates told The LA Times. "I was just very taken aback, in a sense, by that."

Dodgers general manager Brandon Gomes did not comment on the talks, but told The Times that he wished "nothing but the best for Bates and his family."

Reflecting on how things played out, Bates didn't seem to hold any bitter feelings about how it worked out.

"Processing it, I think that there's always a time and a place, and I think that things run their course," Bates said to Lee. "But I have nothing but amazing things to say about the Dodgers organization and people.

"My kids grew up Dodgers, and I grew up a Dodger, as a coach. It's just unfortunate the way it's worked out towards these last few days."

What is next for Aaron Bates and the Dodgers?

With experience in a highly esteemed organization like the Dodgers and as a three-time champion, Bates should land on his feet easily.

In fact, he told the Times that he is already speaking with other teams.

"I'm talking to many different teams, and we're kind of working through some things, and I'll leave it at that for now," he said. "But it's exciting times in that sense."

Regarding the Dodgers, they will likely now either promote internally or bring in someone from another organization, but either way, there will be a fresh voice on the coaching staff.

Changes on successful teams can be tough, but after a disappointing NLCS exit in which the offense went cold, shaking things up could help.

articles.title: Week 9 Preview: From Wentz We Were
articles.summary: Will the Offense Remain Offensive?
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings return home to U.S. Bank Stadium to face the Buffalo Bills in a rematch of the most memorable regular-season game in years: a thrilling 33-30 overtime road win in 2022.

Will the Vikings repeat their magic on Monday Night? Hey, can you believe it's already November? Time sure does fly, doesn't it?

There's not much more to say that I didn't cover a few days ago. To be honest, I'm exhausted by it all. Sitting here in Week 9, still sorting this mess out, is really an indictment of Kevin O'Connell and the entire offensive staff. Things need to be fixed, and fast.

The Kurt Warner film breakdown video below has been circulating here at the DN and across social media over the past few days. To recap, Kyler Murray has made some nice plays, but he's missing far too many opportunities. It simply hasn't been good enough, especially given the weak defenses he's been facing. Per ESPN's Bill Barnwell, Murray's 44.9 QBR through Week 8 ranks just 26th when adjusted for the cupcake units he's faced. In true Vikings fashion, the schedule was set up beautifully for the offense to find its rhythm before things got tougher, and we flushed the opportunity down the toilet. The last time we faced anything that resembled a "good" defense was the Tampa Bay Buccaneers five weeks ago.

As I'm writing this, it's official: Kevin O'Connell announced that Carson Wentz will start Monday night in place of the injured Murray. Max Brosmer will be the backup. Hmmm. Oh, I'll just say it: If Wentz plays well, barring an injury or trade, he'll remain the starter. I believe KOC may have said otherwise, but may I present, as Exhibit 1A, past statements about young quarterbacks and a fella named J.J. McCarthy.

Wentz should be an upgrade over his season in the system, given his proven ability to move the ball efficiently. He passed for over 300 yards twice in four starts last year before KOC famously threw him out there against the Chargers in Week 8, while uttering the famous words of Ivan Drago: "If he dies, he dies."

He also, of course, played essentially two games for us this year, going 23-for-39 (59%) for 276 yards (7.08 avg), 3 TDs, and 0 INTs (though a couple of possible ones were dropped). That's good for a 106.4 QB rating. That's…okay, but he'll need to do more if he's indeed the guy from here on out. Unlike Murray, he does have a proven track record of getting the ball to Justin Jefferson, at least. So that's something. No doubt Jefferson smiled when he heard the news.

Enter the Buffalo Bills, and, will you look at this, another weak defense for us to possibly step on a rake against. Yippee. They rank 23rd in EPA/play, 24th in points allowed (25.9), 24th in total yards allowed (352.1), and 30th in passing yards allowed (254.7). They're better against the run (10th), but that may be more about how easily teams have been able to pass against them.

Wentz should have opportunities against a porous Bills pass defense, so for goodness' sake, let's hope we can finally see some life. The fans need it, and, most of all, an overstressed defense needs it. The pressure to hold teams under 20 to have any shot at winning games, given an offense channeling leather-helmet-era output, has to take its toll.

Brian Flores and company face what may be their toughest challenge to date in containing Josh Allen and the Bills offense. The Lions are great, but Allen's mobility and ability to extend plays add an enormous challenge. While he may not be Jahmyr Gibbs, James Cook III is no slouch, averaging 5.1 yards per carry and 101 yards per game. Their receiving corps is solid, if unspectacular. Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman, and old Viking nemesis D.J. Moore lead the wideouts, while tight end Dalton Kincaid leads the Bills in receiving yards per game (57.3) and can be a real red-zone menace.

But let's be real: the Bills offense is Josh Allen. For my money, he's the league's best quarterback, and he's playing like it. He's leading an attack that's 1st in EPA/play, 2nd in total yards, 2nd in yards per play, 3rd in rushing yards, and 10th in passing yards. They're also near the top of the league in red zone and 3rd-down percentages, respectively.

This is a true strength-vs.-strength battle against the Vikings' defense. They remain 1st in EPA/play, points per game, success rate allowed, Pass EPA/play, and passing yards allowed. They're only 2nd in yards allowed per game. What gives, Flores!?

Of course, we've been vulnerable to the run in a couple of games this year, and the unit's rankings took a hit after giving up a whopping 230 yards to the Lions last week. We're now 17th in rushing yards allowed per game and are giving up 4.5 yards per carry. If my concern level for the offense is a 10, I'd put this at a solid 2 right now. They'll get this straightened out soon enough, but, as noted, this week will bring another challenge.

Indeed, you'd think the two priorities for this week would be, first, to keep Cook contained on early downs, which would repeatedly force Allen and the Bills' offense into the pressure cooker of 3rd-and-long against the blitz and our elite coverage unit. Second, to (as much as possible) keep Allen contained in the pocket in those likely passing situations. If he buys himself time outside the pocket, more often than not you're toast.

Conversely, I'd be shocked if the Bills don't test our shaky run defense early and often in this one to avoid those very scenarios. In addition, what makes the Bills' offense so dangerous is their ability to convert 4th-and-short situations with Allen, who, at over 6' 5" and nearly 240 pounds, is nearly impossible to stuff at the line of scrimmage. This can not only extend drives but also frustrate and demoralize a defense.

If we're to win this one, I can't see us doing it without creating a turnover or two. The good news is that Allen does suffer from a bit of Stafforditis – i.e., elite QBs who are prone to throwing some head-scratching INTs. Hopefully, the pressure Flores will bring will help. James Cook has also had problems holding onto the ball this year, with four fumbles already, so there's that, too.

Wentz starting gives me a bit more confidence we can pull off the upset, but I can't, in good conscience, pick the Vikings to win this game until I see something – anything – that resembles consistency from the offense. Scoring 24 points consistently shouldn't be this difficult with our skill players. Wentz did make the most of the short fields the Packers gave us in Week 1, getting us to 39 points. Sure, there were TD drives of 1 play for 1 yard, 3 plays for 14 yards, and 6 plays for 28 yards. But we also had a 9-play, 83-yard scoring drive! It's like the '98 Vikings and '99 Rams rolled into one!

Holding Allen and the Bills offense under 20 in this game may require Flores to paint another masterpiece like the Week 17 game against the Lions last year at U.S. Bank Stadium. Can it happen? Absolutely. Will it happen? Ehhh, you can't count on it. Regardless, it'd be nice not to have to rely on that every week, wouldn't it?

My guess: Wentz injects some much-needed life into the offense, but we come up short. Reverse psychology initiated.
