articles.title: By the numbers: Ohio State ices out Youngstown State, 89-65
articles.summary: It took awhile, but the dam eventually broke for Ohio State in an 89-65 win over Youngstown State
articles.body:
Alexa, play "Back In the Saddle" by Aerosmith.

For the first time in eight months, Ohio State was back in the Schottenstein Center on Friday night, taking on in-state foe Youngstown State in Ohio State's home opener.

The Buckeyes came into this game 6-0 against the Penguins all-time, with the most recent win coming on November 11, 2024. John Mobley Jr. and Aaron Bradshaw each scored 16 points in Ohio State's 81-47 win.

The aforementioned Mobley made his 55th start in an Ohio State uniform, alongside Justin Pippen, Anthony Thompson, Amare Bynum, and Andrija Jelavic.

Despite Ohio State's obvious advantage in this game both on paper this season and in the all-time series between the two, Jake Diebler said on Thursday afternoon that the Buckeyes would need to be hyper-aware of YSU's guards on the perimeter, especially junior guard Linus Holmstrom. The 6-foot-3 Swedish guard scored 26 points in Youngstown State's season-opening 79-71 win over St. Bonaventure on Monday night, including going 6-for-13 from beyond the arc. Holmstrom was a 39.4% three-point shooter last season.

The aforementioned Holmstrom made an early impact on the game Friday night, knocking down three-pointers on back-to-back possessions 15 seconds apart to give the Penguins a 10-8 lead with 15:17 left in the first half.

Ohio State struggled to shake off the Penguins in the first half, retaking a 21-19 lead on a second-chance bucket by Andrija Jelavic with 8:54 remaining in the opening stanza. The Buckeyes were mauling Youngstown State on the glass, but their first eight offensive rebounds led to just two second-chance points somehow. Ohio State was reading the ball off the rim and beating the Penguins to the glass, but were failing to convert on a bunch of high-percentage looks around the basket.

Back-to-back three-pointers for Youngstown State's Jermaine Coleman put the Penguins back in front, 30-28, with 3:52 remaining in the first half. Jake Diebler called timeout, and immediately out of that timeout Justin Pippen threw the ball to nobody along the baseline for a turnover, and then Amare Bynum fouled Coleman shooting a three-pointer just in front of the Ohio State bench. Coleman hit just one of the three, putting Youngstown State up 31-28 with just over three minutes left in the first half.

Ohio State ripped off a 10-2 run to end the first half, taking a 38-33 lead into the locker room. Mobley scored four and Pippen connected for Ohio State's first three-pointer of the game with 1:36 to go until the halftime break.

The scored stayed within three points in either direction for the first 10 minutes of the second half, with Youngstown State taking the lead multiple times, only for Ohio State to come back moments later. With Ohio State up 55-52 and just under 10 minutes left in the game, Jelavic knocked down a three and dropped in a layup on back-to-back possessions to give Ohio State a 60-52 lead — its biggest margin of the night to that point. Those two buckets put Jelavic at 15 points on the night — a new career-high for the junior from Croatia.

Despite the lid never really coming off the basket from long range at any point, Ohio State was able to separate from Youngstown State over the final 10 minutes, and pulled away for a 89-65 victory at home. John Mobley Jr. recorded his 16th career 20-point game, finishing with 25 on 7-for-9 shooting. Jelavic finished with a career-high 21 points to go along with nine rebounds.

Ohio State picked up its first win of the season Friday night. Here are a few key numbers and statistics from the Buckeyes' victory:

1: Dunk (and technical) for John Mobley Jr.

With just over 10 minutes remaining in the first half, Mobley stole the ball from Coleman near the free throw line and took off the other way like a wide receiver in broken coverage. Mobley, who is generously listed at 6-foot-2 on the Ohio State roster, had never dunked in-game before. With nobody in front of him, he rose up and threw down a two-handed jam, putting Ohio State ahead 19-16.

However, the nearest official determined that Mobley had hung on the rim for a second too long, and assessed the junior a technical foul on his first career dunk. Diebler was incensed, but Youngstown State hit the automatic free throw to get the score back to 19-17 with 10:11 remaining in the first half.

1: First-half three-pointer for Ohio State

Part of the reason Ohio State couldn't shake free of Youngstown State in the first half was their complete inability to knock down a three-pointer. Not a single Buckeye was able to connect from deep until Pippen hit one from the left wing, just in front of the Youngstown State bench with 1:36 remaining in the first half that gave Ohio State a 36-31 lead.

12: First-half offensive rebounds for Ohio State

Last season, Ohio State averaged 9.2 offensive rebounds per game. On Friday night, the Buckeyes had 12 in the first half alone, giving them additional opportunities to score and put some distance between themselves and Youngstown State. Unfortunately, that didn't result in much, as those 12 offensive rebounds turned into just six second-chance points as Ohio State struggled mightily to get the lid off the basket.

Still, when the coaching staff reviews the film from Friday night's game, they'll like to see that Ohio State was creating those second-chance opportunities that they didn't create very often last season.

13: Consecutive points for Ohio State to pull away

The game was nip and tuck for the better part of 30 minutes, and the possibility of Ohio State losing to Youngstown State for the first time ever hung in the air for all 8,000 or so nervous fans. But with 10:20 remaining in the game, Ohio State ripped off a 13-0 run that put them ahead 66-52 and all but sealed this one for the home team. Jelavic was a catalyst during the run, scoring seven of Ohio State's 13 as he marched toward an eventual career-night.

21: Points for Andrija Jelavic – a career-high

The 6-foot-11 transfer from Kentucky notched a career-high in scoring on Friday night, continuing his strong start to the season with 21 points on 10-for-16 shooting. He knocked down a three-pointer for the second consecutive game as well, and seems to have a stranglehold on the starting center spot for Ohio State for now.

articles.title: Klay Thompson Admits He Still Thinks About Returning To Warriors
articles.summary: Heat star Klay Thompson says he's not against reuniting with Stephen Curry.
articles.body:
Not too long ago, Klay Thompson was enjoying historic prosperity on the Golden State Warriors . Alongside Stephen Curry , Draymond Green , and (for some years) Kevin Durant , he helped usher in an era of dominance for the franchise that no basketball fan will soon forget. Now that it's over, however, we can only look back and reflect on what was.

For Klay, who is on the Miami Heat now, so much has changed in a relatively short time. Yesterday, against his former team, he was reminded of that fact, and his response tells us a lot about how he thinks of his time there. According to Klay, he still thinks about his Warriors run and potentially going back there, where it all began.

"A little bit," said Klay after the game . "And I'm so grateful for the support I have in the region. I mean, just going to breakfast this morning and seeing familiar faces. It was awesome. And I'm very, very grateful for the fandom. It really inspires me to keep going."

Of course, Thompson has been out of San Francisco for years now, but it's always a weird experience facing Steph. They once won championships together, and now Klay gets assigned to guard him, just like the opponents they used to beat. Unfortunately for the NBA veteran, Curry got the better of him last night, with a final stat line of 29 points, one rebound, four assists, and one steal on 47.4% shooting from the field.

"It was fun. It was really fun," Thompson said on the matchup with Curry . "Steph's super crafty still to this day, and felt good to block his shot. He made a great up-and-under on me. He had an incredible night, and you know what Steph's doing. I mean, I might not have appreciated it as much as his teammate, 'cause I got to see it every night, so it became normal. But to see it as an opponent, it's incredible. Especially that he's nearing 40 and he moves like a young man, like a young athlete. It's just all the respect in the world for him. He deserves all the accolades, the adulation, the money, and he's just one of one, and the game's going to miss him when he does hang it up."

Klay left the Dubs to pursue a championship on his own terms , but it hasn't panned out as he hoped. After a failed stint with the Dallas Mavericks , he signed with the Heat this summer, only for them to start 3-6. Meanwhile, the Warriors are moving in a positive direction after securing six straight wins . Even Thompson has no choice but to acknowledge their talent.

"The Dubs are very good," Thompson added . "I mean, they have a system in place that has been successful since Steve became the head coach, and never count out the Dubs, especially with Steph and Draymond out there. I mean, Jimmy coming back, Moses coming back. So, strength in numbers has always been their mantra. And I think they'll be a force in the West."

At 36, it's not too late for Klay Thompson to reunite with his former team. With a $5.8 million player option next summer, he could opt out and become a free agent in 2027, setting a clear pathway for him to re-join Steph and Draymond. Plus, with Yaxel Lendeborg and Jimmy Butler , there would be a real chance to make another title run.

Until then, the best Klay can do is reflect on the past and celebrate what he was able to accomplish. As a four-time champion, five-time All-Star, and two-time All-NBA player, his legacy has already been set as an all-time great, and nothing he does going forward will top the heights he reached during his prime.

articles.title: Lewis and Mallory help No. 9 Virginia overcome slow start and beat Northeastern 97-72
articles.summary: Lewis and Mallory each scored 20 points.
articles.body:
CHARLOTTESVILLE, Va. — Sam Lewis and Chance Mallory each scored 20 points as No. 9 Virginia shrugged off a sluggish start and pulled away for a 97-72 win over Northeastern on Friday night.

Thijs De Ridder had 16 points, six rebounds and four assists, and Johann Grunloh, playing on an injured right ankle, added 13 points for the Cavaliers.

Rashad King scored 26 points and guard Louis Bond added 23 for the Huskies, who committed 19 turnovers.

With a matchup against No. 12 Arkansas on tap Sunday, Virginia (2-0) got off to a dreadful start, going 2 for 10 from the field, including 0 for 7 from 3-point range, and committing four turnovers in the first eight minutes.

Virginia didn't take its first lead until Mallory made a layup with 8:23 left in the half. The Cavaliers outscored the Huskies 22-11 over the final nine minutes of the half to take a 38-31 lead to the locker room. The two teams combined for 18 first-half turnovers, 11 by Northeastern.

But a dominant showing in the second half allowed Virginia to rest its starters for the final six minutes. That figures to be important, considering the Cavaliers are getting the bulk of their scoring from the four key players they retained from last year's 30-win squad.

De Ridder, Grunloh, Lewis and Mallory combined for 69 points. Reserve Elijah Gertrude, another returner from last season, had 10 points and five rebounds.

Virginia shot 61.3% from the floor and went 6 for 14 from 3-point range in the second half.

Northeastern: Hosts Harvard on Tuesday night.

Virginia: Plays No. 12 Arkansas on Sunday at Capital One Arena in Washington.

articles.title: Knicks organization responds to Tyler Kolek and Miles McBride questioning Taylor Swift’s fandom
articles.summary: The Knicks stars went viral for their comments about Taylor Swift.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks have responded to Tyler Kolek and Miles McBride's recent comments about Taylor Swift that questioned her allegiance to the New York team.

Kolek and McBride made an appearance on the NBA 2K League TikTok livestream this week when they were asked, "Who's the fakest celeb fan you've seen courtside?"

McBride responded quickly, presuming how his teammate's response would unfold online, "I would agree…Swifties not gonna like that answer."

Kolek agreed with McBride's evaluation of his answer, "I'm gonna get some hate…I guess she's got a lot going on…can't come all the time…but it's a little performative."

In the Knicks guard's defense, he did acknowledge that given her celebrity status, she has a super busy schedule and cannot attend games very often.

The Knicks organization responded to Kolek and McBride's comments with a statement to Entertainment Weekly on Nov. 6.

"Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years, has a long history with Madison Square Garden, and we are incredibly appreciative of her support of the organization."

Swift's most recent appearance in Madison Square Garden to cheer on the team was for Game 4 of the NBA Finals when the Knicks faced the San Antonio Spurs. She sat courtside with friends Alana and Este Haim as well as Mariska Hargitay, where they all rocked custom shirts to cheer on the Knicks.

The last time she was at MSG was ironically not basketball-related. She said "I do" to Travis Kelce on July 3 in front of 1,000 of their star-studded guests.

Despite the comments that McBride and Kolek made questioning her Knicks fandom, the superstar has been sighted at home games since she moved to New York City in 2014.

Kolek and McBride sharing their grievances on Swift's "performative" attendance follows their teammate Jose Alvarado expressing that he wants to see her at more games this season.

"That's a surreal superstar, and I was happy she was cheering us on," the Knicks point guard told Us Weekly back in June. "And [she] seemed like she was having a good time, and we won, so even better."

Alvarado told the outlet that, "She got to come more often."

Kolek and McBride have not reacted to the Knicks' statement at this time.

articles.title: Brandon Ingram is 'pretty close' to making debut with L.A. Clippers: Latest injury update
articles.summary: Brandon Ingram said he's "pretty close" to making his Clippers debut.
articles.body:
Brandon Ingram is working his way back and is close to his debut with the Los Angeles Clippers .

The two-time All-Star has been the biggest absence for the team this season, considering he will be an immediate starter upon his return.

He is recovering from right heel surgery he had in May. He is also dealing with a partially torn Achilles tendon.

"I'm pretty close," Ingram told reporters during media availability on Friday. "I've been on the floor a little bit more than I've been in the past. I didn't have a summer to have 5-on-5, move at all, but I'm gaining that confidence right now."

The Clippers acquired Ingram as one of the primary trade assets in the package sent over by the Toronto Raptors for Kawhi Leonard during the offseason.

Ingram told reporters he was initially supposed to have a bone removed from his heel, but the doctors found the partially torn Achilles during that procedure. While sidelined, he's remained close to the team and appreciates the players' efforts.

"I actually want to commend those guys because everybody is in new positions and asked to do more," Ingram said. "So the guys are trying. They're playing really, really good defense."

See the coolest sneakers of the NBA season

Ingram's return would be welcomed, especially on the offensive end of the floor. The All-Star led Toronto with 21.5 points and was third in rebounds (5.6) last season. He started 77 games for the Raptors.

"They're trying to figure it out on the offensive end," Ingram said. "When I come in, I want to play make, make it a little bit easier for guys to catch and shoot, and not have to make so many decisions. And be able to, when it gets down to it, be able to score."

Ingram already had a level of familiarity with head coach Tyronn Lue and assistant coach Jeff Van Gundy from playing for Team USA during the 2023 FIBA World Cup.

Ingram, center Yanic Konan Niederhäuser and Max Strus, who has the ability to play as both a guard and forward, were recalled on Nov. 2. The trio participated in a weekend assignment with the team's G-League affiliate.

Konan Niederhäuser is working his way back from right Lisfranc surgery. Strus was recovering from a partial tear to his right plantar fascia.

"Max came back and had a big impact on the team," Ingram said. "He's made the team better. Yanic is coming back soon.

"... As a full team, I think we're gonna mesh well. And we'll be a little better than we have been. But in these games that we lost, we've been right in the game. Just fix a few mistakes and we can win those games."

The Clippers won the season opener against the Sacramento Kings before losing seven straight. Los Angeles will host the New Orleans Pelicans on Nov. 8.

articles.title: Mets re-sign journeyman pitcher Robert Stock to 1-year contract
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — The New York Mets re-signed pitcher Robert Stock to a one-year contract Friday.Stock, who turns 37 this month, made seven starts and one reli...
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — The New York Mets re-signed pitcher Robert Stock to a one-year contract Friday.

Stock, who turns 37 this month, made seven starts and one relief appearance for the last-place Mets in 2026. He went 1-3 with a 5.93 ERA over 30 1/3 innings during a comeback season.

The right-hander earned his first major league win since 2019 with San Diego when he threw 5 1/3 shutout innings Aug. 31 in a 3-2 victory at Tampa Bay. He was placed on the 15-day injured list Sept. 16, retroactive to Sept. 13, because of numbness in his fingers and didn't pitch the rest of the season.

Stock said he was on medication for the condition, a byproduct of the thoracic outlet syndrome surgery he underwent in March. He said he would usually begin to experience numbness after throwing about 60 or 70 pitches in a game.

Stock has pitched for eight big league organizations as well as in South Korea and Mexico and for the independent Long Island Ducks. He is 3-7 with a 5.20 ERA in 65 major league games, including 10 starts, for the Padres, Red Sox, Cubs and Mets.

In other news, the Mets announced Thursday they will wear a memorial patch on the sleeve of their uniforms in honor of Jerry Koosman next season. Koosman, a two-time All-Star who pitched the 1969 Miracle Mets to a World Series championship, died Sunday at age 83.

articles.title: Old Tappan football dominates West Morris to reach sectional final

articles.body:
OLD TAPPAN - Zach Miceli completed his first 10 passes, and the Old Tappan senior did not throw his one and only incompletion until late in the third quarter.

The Golden Knights scored on their first six possessions and rolled to a running-clock, 43-21 victory over West Morris on Nov. 6 in a North 1, Group 3 sectional football semifinal.

Miceli threw for 244 yards and three touchdowns in three quarters to lead unbeaten Old Tappan, ranked No. 1 in the North Jersey Public Super 20 and No. 4 in the USA TODAY NETWORK New Jersey Super 25.

Miceli threw first-half TDs of 60 and 50 yards to senior receiver Leo Etter and a 27-yard score to senior running back Nick Blanchard to help Old Tappan (10-0) build a 29-7 halftime lead.

"We've got some guys who are dangerous kids in the pass game, and our quarterback is obviously who he is," Old Tappan coach Brian Dunn said of the three-year starter.

Blanchard scored on third-quarter runs of 1 and 12 yards to extend the Golden Knights' lead to 43-7 and trigger the running clock.

Run-heavy West Morris (7-4) scored its three TDs on the ground. Junior running back Deacon Frayne scored on a 9-yard run in the second quarter to trim the deficit to 15-7

articles.title: Oklahoma gets key players back in latest availability report
articles.summary: Eli Bowen, Rocky Beers and Jer'Michael Carter are all set to return, while Peyton Bowen remains questionable.
articles.body:
One of the biggest storylines for the Oklahoma Sooners this season has been the number of injuries the team has faced. For the third year in a row, the Sooners have had a plethora of injuries to key players.

That is no different against the Florida Gators on Saturday. In the latest availability report , the Sooners have eight players listed as out, one as doubtful, one as questionable and two as probable. The Sooners will be without Ryan Fodje, Cole Sullivan and Jacobe Johnson for sure, as well as likely being without Eddy Pierre-Louis.

Peyton Bowen is listed as questionable, so they could be without their star safety. On the bright side, Eli Bowen, Jake Maikkula, Jer'Michael Carter and Rocky Beers are all back this week. The Sooners may also get Elijah Thomas back.

The injury situation remains a big concern for Oklahoma as it heads into one of its toughest road environments of the season. Losing a potential difference-maker like Peyton Bowen would be a major blow to the Sooners' secondary, while the absences along the offensive and defensive lines could also test the team's depth. With so many players unavailable, Oklahoma will need contributions from its next group of players to keep Florida's offense in check.

Still, the return of several players provides a boost for a team that has struggled to stay healthy throughout the season. Getting Eli, Maikkula, Carter and Beers back gives the Sooners more options, and Thomas could provide another welcome addition if he is cleared to play. Oklahoma will need every available contribution as it looks to overcome its injury challenges and leave Gainesville with a win.

articles.title: Shenendehowa girls' volleyball continues Section 2 title streak
articles.summary: Shenendehowa sophomores Melanie Tubbs and Claire Siska combined for 18 kills, junior Hadley Ennist added 10 kills and 11 assists, and senior Ava Los chipped...
articles.body:
SARATOGA SPRINGS - The Shenendehowa girls' volleyball team boasts a powerhouse up front, with several weapons the Mustangs can call on to make an impact.

In Friday's Section 2 Class AAA championship, Shenendehowa's potent offense was the focus once again as the top-seeded Mustangs swept past No. 2 Saratoga Springs in straight sets 25-13, 25-14, 25-16, at Saratoga Springs High School.

"It makes it so fun because the defense doesn't really have one person to focus on," Shenendehowa coach Lori Kessler said. "They have to focus on three hitting options at all times, and running a 6-2 with two great setters, they're spreading it out. It's such a great part of our offense."

Shenendehowa sophomores Melanie Tubbs and Claire Siska combined for 18 kills, junior Hadley Ennist added 10 kills and 11 assists, and senior Ava Los chipped in five kills.

Shenendehowa, the top-ranked team in the state Class AAA poll, pushed its sectional title win streak to six with. The four most recent championships have come in Class AAA since the state expanded to a six-classification system.

"It's a completely new team than what we've had in the past," Ennist said. "It's a ton of younger girls and some seniors. It's just such a big mix and honestly, we're doing a great job together. It's so fun to be able to play with such a variety of ages and abilities out there."

Shenendehowa trailed 6-5 in the second set, but used a pair of runs to gain control. The Mustangs used a 7-0 spurt to grab a 12-6 lead, and Ennist set up sophomore Leah Alfandre for a kill to cap a 5-1 run which provided Shenendehowa its first double-digit lead of the set, 17-7.

"Those were really big for us, especially in a game this competitive," Ennist said. "If you do get into a little bit of a rut, you still have so much time to come out of it, and I think we did a really great job of getting that lead."

Shenendehowa freshman setter Kyli Kessler, the coach's daughter, turned in a stellar all-around performance. Kessler finished with 19 assists, 12 service points, including a pair of aces, and nine digs.

"She works hard year-round on her game," Lori Kessler said of her daughter. "I think that she really wanted to prove herself this season, and I think that her being surrounded by the girls, by the great passing and the great hitters, makes her job a little bit easier for her. But regardless, she's still an everyday hard worker that if something feels off, she's the first one out there that wants to fix it and make it better for everybody."

Digs Shenendehowa sophomore defensive specialist Avery Young recorded.

Kills Saratoga junior standout outside hitter Ali Sherman totaled.

The Mustangs (17-0) will take on the Section 3 winner in a regional final at 7 p.m. Friday, Nov. 13 at Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake High School.

The Blue Streaks end their season with an 11-7 showing.

articles.title: Wild's Brock Faber Opens Up About 'Scary' Fractured Skull Injury, Updates Rehab Process
articles.summary: Minnesota Wild defenseman Brock Faber said he stayed in the preseason game during which a puck fractured his skull because he didn't initially feel significant pain from the injury.
articles.body:
Minnesota Wild defenseman Brock Faber said he stayed in the preseason game during which a puck fractured his skull because he didn't initially feel significant pain from the injury.

Faber was hit by a shot from the Dallas Stars midway through the second period of a Sept. 25 preseason game. He played the rest of the period before exiting the game and later undergoing surgery.

"When the initial thing happened, I didn't anything of it, because it was such a slow shot," Faber told reporters Friday. "They all talked to me, and came down to the bench, and were asking all the questions. I told them, actually, 'I swear I'm actually good. There's nothing wrong with my head.'

"And then I guess I was wrong. But really, it didn't hurt at all. So that's why I kept playing."

Wild coach John Hynes said immediately after Faber's injury the defenseman had been hit just below the edge of his helmet above his ear.

Faber said there was limited swelling but that "things progressively got worse" after the second period. Doctors discovered the fracture after Faber underwent a CT scan at the hospital that night.

"I didn't really let myself think any other way than I'll be playing for a month," Faber said about his initial reaction to his diagnosis.

Faber said he felt "completely fine" within a few days after surgery but was forced to initially remain inactive as part of his recovery process.

"It was scary there for a little bit, but to be honest I don't really care to go into too much detail," Faber said. "I would rather not have the whole world know that. But I got treated so well, and it could have been a lot worse if, one, if I got hit harder in that spot, and two, if I didn't get the medical attention that I did."

"The thing, as a whole, I'm just so glad to put it in the past. It's so good to be back."

Faber's talk with reporters came the day after he rejoined Wild practice for the first time since suffering his injury.

Hynes said Thursday Faber had been medically cleared to return but wasn't "physically" ready to play yet.

He added Faber would be traveling with the team on their upcoming three-game road trip, which starts Tuesday at the Montreal Canadiens and continues Thursday in Toronto and Saturday in Boston.

The Wild (11-3-3) went into a Friday night matchup with the San Jose Sharks holding a lead over the Central Division. Minnesota will hope reuniting Faber and Quinn Hughes on their top pairing in the near future will help this team contend for the top of the Western Conference down the stretch of the season.

articles.title: Khawaja claims entire Australia team knew about 2018 ball-tampering scandal
articles.summary: The ‘Sandpapergate’ scandal saw ⁠Australia scuffing the ball with sandpaper in the March 2018 test in Cape Town.
articles.body:
Former opener Usman Khawaja claimed on Saturday that the entire Australian team knew about the 2018 “Sandpapergate” scandal in Cape Town and said they also employed the tactic during the previous Test at Port Elizabeth.

Captain Steve Smith, his deputy David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were sent home in disgrace and found by a Cricket Australia investigation to be the only three players with prior knowledge of the ball-tampering plot .

Smith was banned for a year and sacked as skipper, Warner was suspended for 12 months and stripped of all leadership roles, while Bancroft was slapped with a nine-month ban. Head coach Darren Lehmann was cleared of direct involvement but resigned ⁠soon after the series.

But Khawaja, who retired this year after 88 Tests, told The Sydney Morning Herald everyone had prior knowledge.

“It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us,” he said ahead of the release of his autobiography next week, where a chapter is dedicated to the issue.

Bowlers Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon all denied publicly in 2021 that they knew about it.

Khawaja said he spoke in the dressing room after the Cape Town Test, urging the team to take collective responsibility, rather than scapegoating Warner, Smith and Bancroft.

“In an ideal world, I don’t want to do this,” Khawaja said.

“I don’t want to be the one who comes out and talks about the truth. The issue is that I genuinely thought after eight years the truth would have been out by now.

“Maybe I thought Davey [Warner] would have exposed it, or someone else would have talked about it more. I just didn’t think it was going to come down to this.”

In the book, according to the newspaper, Khawaja recounts that discussions about ways to rough up the ball were also held in the dressing room during the second Test at Port Elizabeth, now known as Gqeberha.

It culminated in the discovery that sandpaper was effective, and at this point Smith allegedly walked away, saying he did not want to know about it.

Bancroft then allegedly volunteered to use sandpaper in South Africa’s first innings in Gqeberha, where the ball swung significantly.

Cricket Australia said in a statement it was “comfortable” with the findings of its original investigation, but remained open to new evidence.

“There has been a great deal of speculation in the eight years since the 2018 Cape Town Test, including extensive media coverage throughout last month’s series in South Africa,” it said.

“During this time there has been the ongoing opportunity to present any relevant information, and this remains the case.

“All relevant information presented to CA to date has been properly considered and we remain comfortable with the findings of our integrity process.”

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz saves match points to reach Paris Masters semifinals
articles.summary: Seven-time Grand Slam champion Alcaraz is through to the Paris Masters semifinals for the first time in his career.
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz produced another miracle in the French capital as the seven-time Grand Slam champion fended off two match points to beat Taylor Fritz and reach the Paris Masters semifinals on Friday.

The 23-year-old fought back to win 6-7 (10/12), 7-5, 6-3 and advance to the last four of the event for the first time.

He will next take on former world number two Casper Ruud on Saturday after the Norwegian eliminated Portuguese lucky loser Nuno Borges 7-6 (7/5), 6-4.

In scenes reminiscent of his iconic French Open final comeback win over Jannik Sinner last season, when he saved three championship points, Alcaraz again wowed the crowd in Paris as he snatched another improbable victory from the jaws of defeat.

“Probably this match is going to be one of the most special matches that I ever played, and I’m going to remember this match for a long time,” Alcaraz told reporters.

Despite only playing one match en route to the quarterfinals, Alcaraz showed no signs of rust as he seized his first break opportunity in the fifth game of the opening set, whipping a forehand passing shot around the stranded Fritz.

The Spaniard’s serve then started to wobble, and Fritz pounced to break to love and level at 5-5.

In a tie-break of thrills and spills, both players had set points come and go before Alcaraz dumped a forehand wide to cede the opener to the Californian.

After recovering from 0-40 to hold early in the second set, Alcaraz pointed to his ear and held his fist aloft in a bid to get the Parisian crowd going – the first but not last callback to his five-set Roland Garros epic .

But he continued to struggle to make inroads on Fritz’s serve, and it was the American who produced the first break of the set in the seventh game.

Alcaraz staved off a match point and then secured a hold that kept his campaign alive with a sensational backhand slice from well wide of his own tramlines.

“After that game… I started to enjoy it because I just thought I pulled off great shots, great points; I started to smile; I started to bring the energy from the people to the match,” the former world number one said.

A fine passing shot saved a second match point in the next game before Alcaraz wiped out the break and then completed his Houdini act by breaking Fritz again to set up a decider.

The rampant Murcian had a chokehold on the match and went in front 3-1 in the third set when Fritz pushed a volley wide.

Alcaraz still had to save break points in a match that always threatened another twist but, as it rumbled towards a conclusion, he brought up two match points on his own serve, sealing the first with a powerful forehand that Fritz could only get a frame on.

Earlier, Ben Shelton edged Tommy Paul 6-4, 4-6, 6-3 in an all-American quarterfinal.

The defeats for Paul and Fritz ended both players’ hopes of qualifying for the ATP Finals, with American Frances Tiafoe and Spanish 20-year-old Rafael Jodar now set to make their debuts at the season-ending showpiece, which will run from November 15-22 in Turin.

“Frances has had an outstanding year. One of my best friends, and to see him make Turin for the first time is amazing,” Shelton said of the 28-year-old Finals debutant.

Shelton will meet Luca Van Assche in the last four after the Frenchman ended Australian Rinky Hijikata’s fairytale run from qualifying to the last eight.
